description: The physics of heat, temperature, energy, and entropy. Covers the laws of thermodynamics, thermodynamic potentials, kinetic theory, and an introduction to statistical mechanics.

concepts.title: Thermal Equilibrium and the Zeroth Law
learning_objectives: State the zeroth law of thermodynamics and define thermal equilibrium
Define temperature operationally via the zeroth law
Convert between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin temperature scales

concepts.title: Equations of State
learning_objectives: State the ideal gas law PV = nRT and identify its assumptions
Apply the van der Waals equation as a model for real gases
Plot and interpret P-V, P-T, and V-T diagrams for ideal and real gases

concepts.title: Thermal Expansion and Calorimetry
learning_objectives: Calculate linear and volumetric thermal expansion
Define specific heat capacity and latent heat
Solve calorimetry problems using conservation of energy

concepts.title: Work, Heat, and Internal Energy
learning_objectives: Define thermodynamic work as W = ∫P dV and compute it for quasi-static processes
Distinguish between heat and work as path-dependent energy transfers
State the first law of thermodynamics: ΔU = Q − W

concepts.title: Thermodynamic Processes for Ideal Gases
learning_objectives: Analyze isothermal, isobaric, isochoric, and adiabatic processes for ideal gases
Derive the adiabatic relation PVᵞ = constant from the first law
Compute Q, W, and ΔU for each type of process

concepts.title: Heat Capacity and Equipartition
learning_objectives: Derive Cᵥ and Cₚ for an ideal gas and show Cₚ − Cᵥ = nR
Apply the equipartition theorem to predict heat capacities from degrees of freedom
Explain the failure of classical equipartition at low temperatures (qualitative quantum preview)

concepts.title: Heat Engines, Refrigerators, and the Second Law
learning_objectives: State the Kelvin-Planck and Clausius formulations of the second law
Define and compute the efficiency of a heat engine and the coefficient of performance of a refrigerator
Prove that no engine operating between two reservoirs can exceed Carnot efficiency

concepts.title: The Carnot Cycle
learning_objectives: Describe the four steps of the Carnot cycle on a P-V diagram
Derive the Carnot efficiency η = 1 − Tᶜ/Tₕ
Explain the significance of the Carnot cycle as the most efficient cycle between two temperatures

concepts.title: Entropy
learning_objectives: Define entropy via the Clausius inequality: dS ≥ δQ/T
Compute entropy changes for reversible and irreversible processes
State the entropy form of the second law: ΔS_universe ≥ 0

concepts.title: Entropy of an Ideal Gas and the T-S Diagram
learning_objectives: Derive the entropy of an ideal gas as a function of T and V (or T and P)
Plot thermodynamic cycles on T-S diagrams and interpret enclosed area as net heat
Compute entropy changes for mixing, free expansion, and phase transitions

concepts.title: Enthalpy, Helmholtz, and Gibbs Free Energy
learning_objectives: Define enthalpy H = U + PV, Helmholtz free energy F = U − TS, and Gibbs free energy G = H − TS
Identify the natural variables for each potential (U: S,V; H: S,P; F: T,V; G: T,P)
Determine the appropriate potential for a given set of constraints

concepts.title: Maxwell Relations
learning_objectives: Derive the four Maxwell relations from the thermodynamic potentials
Use Maxwell relations to express difficult-to-measure quantities in terms of measurable ones
Apply Maxwell relations to derive relationships between Cₚ, Cᵥ, and the equation of state

concepts.title: Phase Transitions and the Clausius-Clapeyron Equation
learning_objectives: Describe first-order and continuous (second-order) phase transitions
Derive and apply the Clausius-Clapeyron equation dP/dT = L/(TΔV)
Interpret phase diagrams and identify triple points and critical points

concepts.title: Molecular Speed Distributions
learning_objectives: Derive the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution from probability arguments
Compute the most probable speed, mean speed, and root-mean-square speed
Relate the macroscopic pressure and temperature to molecular kinetic energy

concepts.title: Mean Free Path and Transport Phenomena
learning_objectives: Derive the mean free path λ = 1/(nσ√2) from molecular collision cross-sections
Relate mean free path to viscosity, thermal conductivity, and diffusion coefficients
Apply kinetic theory to explain macroscopic transport phenomena

concepts.title: Microstates, Macrostates, and the Boltzmann Entropy
learning_objectives: Define microstates and macrostates for a thermodynamic system
State the Boltzmann entropy formula S = k_B ln Ω
Calculate the number of microstates for simple systems (two-state, Einstein solid)

concepts.title: The Canonical Ensemble and Partition Function
learning_objectives: Define the canonical ensemble for a system in thermal contact with a reservoir
Define and compute the partition function Z = Σ e^{−Eᵢ/k_BT}
Derive thermodynamic quantities (U, S, F) from the partition function

concepts.title: Applications of the Partition Function
learning_objectives: Compute the partition function and thermodynamic properties of the ideal gas
Analyze the two-state paramagnet using the partition function
Derive the Planck distribution for blackbody radiation from the partition function (preview)

concepts.title: Identical Particles and Quantum Statistics
learning_objectives: Distinguish between bosons and fermions based on spin and symmetry requirements
Derive the Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac distribution functions
Recover the classical Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution as a high-temperature limit

concepts.title: Blackbody Radiation and the Planck Distribution
learning_objectives: Derive the Planck spectral energy density from Bose-Einstein statistics for photons
Derive the Stefan-Boltzmann law and Wien's displacement law from the Planck distribution
Explain how Planck's distribution resolves the ultraviolet catastrophe

concepts.title: The Fermi Gas and Degenerate Matter
learning_objectives: Define the Fermi energy and Fermi temperature for a free electron gas
Compute the density of states and total energy of a degenerate Fermi gas at T = 0
Apply Fermi gas theory to electrons in metals and degenerate stellar matter (white dwarfs)

modules.title: The Third Law and Low-Temperature Physics

concepts.title: The Third Law of Thermodynamics
learning_objectives: State the Nernst form and the Planck form of the third law
Explain the unattainability of absolute zero
Apply the third law to determine absolute entropies of substances

concepts.title: Bose-Einstein Condensation
learning_objectives: Derive the critical temperature for Bose-Einstein condensation in an ideal gas
Describe the macroscopic occupation of the ground state below T_c
Discuss experimental realizations of BEC in dilute atomic gases

projects.title: Analyzing a Real Engine Cycle
projects.description: Model the Otto cycle (gasoline engine) and the Diesel cycle as sequences of thermodynamic processes. Compute efficiency as a function of compression ratio and compare to Carnot efficiency.
learning_objectives: Model each step of a real engine cycle as an ideal thermodynamic process
Compute work, heat, and efficiency for the full cycle
Compare real engine efficiency to the Carnot limit and explain the discrepancy

projects.title: Monte Carlo Simulation of the Ising Model
projects.description: Simulate a 2D Ising model using the Metropolis algorithm. Measure magnetization and energy as functions of temperature and observe the phase transition near the critical temperature.
learning_objectives: Implement the Metropolis algorithm for statistical sampling
Measure thermodynamic observables from simulation data
Identify the critical temperature and characterize the phase transition

projects.title: Deriving the Stefan-Boltzmann Law from Planck's Distribution
projects.description: Starting from the Planck spectral energy density, integrate over all frequencies to derive the Stefan-Boltzmann law. Compute the Stefan-Boltzmann constant in terms of fundamental constants.
learning_objectives: Set up and evaluate the integral of the Planck distribution over all frequencies
Evaluate the integral using standard results for ∫x³/(eˣ−1) dx
Express the Stefan-Boltzmann constant in terms of k_B, ℏ, and c
